what_its_for: Giltuss Diabetic EX is an expectorant and cough suppressant used to relieve chest congestion and cough caused by colds, the flu, or other breathing irritations. The expectorant (guaifenesin) helps thin and loosen mucus in your airways so it is easier to cough up. The cough suppressant (dextromethorphan) helps reduce the urge to cough. This formula is specially made without sugar, alcohol, or artificial dyes, making it a safer option for people with diabetes.
how_to_take: Take this medication by mouth as directed. You may take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, taking it with food or a full glass of water may help. Drink plenty of fluids while using this medicine — staying well hydrated helps thin mucus and makes the medicine work better. Use the measuring device that comes with the product to measure your dose carefully. Do not use a regular kitchen spoon, as it may not give you the correct amount.
dosing: Always follow the directions on the package label or your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions. For adults and children 12 years and older, the typical dose is 10 mL (2 teaspoons) every 4 hours as needed. Do not take more than 6 doses (60 mL) in 24 hours. For children under 12 years, ask your doctor or pharmacist for the correct dose. Do not exceed the recommended dose.
missed_dose: This medicine is usually taken only as needed, so you may not be on a regular dosing schedule. If your doctor has told you to take it on a set schedule and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom, near a sink, or in hot or humid places. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely by following your local guidelines or using a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not take more than the recommended dose. Avoid taking other cough, cold, or allergy medicines at the same time without checking with your pharmacist or doctor first, as many of these products contain similar ingredients that could lead to an overdose. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication, as it can increase drowsiness and side effects. Be cautious when driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, since dextromethorphan can cause dizziness or drowsiness in some people. Do not use this medicine if you have taken a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) — such as phenelzine, tranylcypromine, selegiline, or linezolid — within the past 14 days, as this combination can cause a serious reaction.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek medical help right away if you experience: a cough that lasts more than 7 days or keeps coming back; a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache; difficulty breathing or shortness of breath; severe dizziness, confusion, or unusual drowsiness; nausea or vomiting that is severe; or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also talk to your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or if they get worse after a few days of use. Diabetic patients should monitor blood sugar levels as usual and report any unexpected changes to their healthcare provider.
when_it_works: Guaifenesin (the expectorant) starts to help loosen mucus within 30 minutes and works best when you drink plenty of fluids. Dextromethorphan (the cough suppressant) typically begins to reduce cough within 15 to 30 minutes after you take a dose. The full benefit of each dose generally lasts about 4 hours. Most coughs due to a common cold improve within 5 to 7 days. If your cough is not better after 7 days, please speak with your doctor.
special_populations: Diabetic patients: This formula is sugar-free and alcohol-free, making it appropriate for people managing diabetes. However, continue to monitor your blood sugar as directed by your healthcare team. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Ask your doctor before using this medicine to make sure it is safe for you and your baby. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of dextromethorphan, such as dizziness or confusion. Use with caution and consider consulting your doctor before use. Children under 12 years: Do not use in children under 12 years without specific guidance from a pediatrician, as dosing must be adjusted for age and weight. Patients with liver or kidney disease: Speak with your doctor or pharmacist before using this product.
